doc: What each skill and agent this plugin ships is FOR, as routing data, and the engine's own built-in providers. The prompt router reads it; nothing in src/ names a component. `provides` is what a component can satisfy, `signals` are words that make it relevant, `requiresSignal` means it is only recommended when one of those words is in the prompt, `needs` names the capabilities it cannot work without and `optional` the ones it can use when the task names a provider for them -- capabilities, never a server or a tool: the resolver finds who provides each. An agent row's `via` names the shipped skills whose playbook dispatches it (0.5.0): such an agent is chosen only as a provider one of those skills pulls in, never straight from a prompt's words, and the skill's line names it; an agent with no `via` may be dispatched by the session itself. `reactsTo` (0.6.0) names the facts about a session's work its own playbook handles -- words of src/routing/facts.mjs FACTS, derived by the engine and never read off a prompt -- and a fact that holds counts for it as one of its signals would. `builtins` are what the engine answers itself, `run` saying how; `implicit` marks one the session already has, which the router never adds as a line. test/resources.test.mjs holds one row per shipped skill and agent, and test/activation-catalog.test.mjs holds every `via` to a skill whose playbook names the agent.
